A series of Ti- y Nb (15, 32, 38 wt%) alloys ingots with different oxygen contents (0, 0.2, 0.5 wt%) were fabricated by vacuum arc melting under argon atmosphere using Ti sponge (99.7%), high purity Nb (99.9%) and TiO2 powder (99.9%). To guarantee the ingot uniformity, samples were melted repeatedly for 6 times.
The ingots were subjected to homogenization at 1273 K for 7.2 ks in the Ar gas atmosphere, followed by water quenching.
Then the ingots were cold rolled (oxygen content was 0 or 0.2 wt%) or hot rolled (oxygen content was 0.5 wt%) at 1023 K to a thickness of 1.5 mm with a thickness reduction of 85%.
These sheets were solutionized at 1173 K for 1.8 ks followed by water quenching.
